title: F4: Port Compx mouse protocol + CLI
description: Port crates/proto-mouse from ../oh-my-gravastar-upstream/orbit-gravastar/src/protocol/mouse.rs (476 lines, MIT, has unit tests to port). Spec: docs in upstream docs/protocol-mouse.md. Transport: VID 0x3554, dongle PIDs F54B F575 F548 F577, wired F576 F549, usage page 0xFF02, report id 8, 16-byte payload [cmd,status,addrHi,addrLo,len,data*10,cksum]; checksum = (0x08 + sum bytes 0..14) & 0xFF == 0x55 i.e. byte15 = (0x4D - sum) & 0xFF. One request in flight; mouse may push unsolicited 0x0A reports. Commands: 01 identify (CID 18=GravaStar; MID 1-2 PAW3395 26k DPI, MID 3-5 PAW3950 32k), 03 online, 04 battery (voltage->percent table of 21 entries), 07 write flash, 08 read flash, 0E profile, 12 mouse fw, 1D dongle fw. Flash map: polling@0, stage count@2, current@4, LOD@10, DPI@12+4i, DPI color@44+4i, buttons@96+4i, light@160, debounce@169, motion sync@171, sleep@173 (x10s units 1,3,6,12,18,30,60,90), angle snap@175, ripple@177, light-off-moving@179, sensor mode@185. Scalars stored as [v, 0x55-v]; records end with check byte summing to 0x55. WRITABLE allowlist of 15 ranges - refuse everything else. NEVER implement: 05/06 pairing, 09 factory reset, 31 RF, B0-B7 bootloader. CLI: omg mouse info|battery|fw|config|get|set <field> --yes; DPI encode (raw=dpi/50-1 or /100-1 high range), clamp per sensor; wireless wake handling per OmaGravastar research/wake_and_battery.py. mouse-protocol/src/drivers/gravastar/hid.ts has TS reference + products.ts ID table. Unit tests: packet checksum vectors, DPI roundtrip, voltage curve (port from upstream tests).

title: F6: SparkPlayJoy 6x21 analog travel reader
description: Depends F2+F1. Implement crates/proto-sparkplayjoy (new crate or module in proto-he) per docs/protocol-sparkplayjoy.md (research agent writes it; fallback: HallJoy/docs/research/GRAVASTAR_MERCURY_V75_FIRMWARE_STATIC_ANALYSIS_2026-08-22.md + aula_win60he_protocol.h/.cpp in ../oh-my-gravastar-upstream/HallJoy). Framed protocol on usage 0xFFA0:0001: request 5C <len> <cmd> <cksum> <payload>; response cmd = request|0x80; checksum low byte of (35+0x5C+len+cmd+last-payload-byte); long responses continue over multiple 64-byte reports (65-byte Win32 buffer, report id 0). Fn function = 0xF001 -> extended keycode 0x409; Menu = HID 0x0065; never truncate Fxxx. CLI: omg kb travel-matrix [--watch] --json emitting {row,col,travel_um,actuated}. Verify on HE keyboard; if none available mark hardware-pending in code docs.

title: keymap-base-guard: whole-table writes must abort on a short/unknown base read
description:
Violates AGENTS.md §Safety 6/7 (added 2026-11-25 after the Fn-layer incident).

Evidence:
- web/src/remap.ts writeChanges(): `const entries = app.snapshot?.keymaps.get(arg) ?? []` then `values = entries.map(...)`. An empty/failed base read sends an all-zero table; read-back verify passes because the device stored exactly that. Silent layer wipe.
- Rust CLI already guards (crates/omg/src/main.rs:4454 requires values.len() == current.len() for keymap-file writes). The web path has no equivalent.
- web/src/advkeys.ts:623 slices this.keymap and writes it back — same class.

Acceptance criteria:
1. A shared guard: base read must be non-empty, the expected length, and every slot must decode to a KNOWN tag (or be carried opaque per §Safety 7).
2. remap.ts / advkeys.ts / macro bind paths abort with a clear message before any byte is sent when the guard fails.
3. Unit tests with a mock session: empty base, short base, base containing an unknown tag.
4. No fallback to `?? []` or 0 anywhere on a whole-table write path.

title: khub916-tag8: reverse the Fn-layer tag 0x08 action encoding
description:
Tag 0x08 is undocumented (docs/protocol-behaviors.md §1.1, docs/protocol-khub916.md §6) yet carries the entire K1 Pro Fn layer.

Live values (2026-11-25, omg kb916 keys --layer 1):
  0x08000000 |  0x08000001 R_Shift  0x08020000 Tab   0x08020001 /?
  0x08030100 F6/Up  0x08030200 F5/Down  0x08030201 >.  0x08030300 ?
  0x08040001 <,  0x08040100 Right  0x08040200 Left
No case 8 in vendor be(), absent from the Ca pool -> the vendor UI cannot assign these, but firmware acts on them.

Questions to answer:
1. Is 08 xx a row/secondary-layer reference, a media function, or a lighting action? The 0x08 02/03/04 nibble and trailing 00/01 look like a matrix row + index, not a HID usage.
2. Why do slots 4 (L_Shift) and 79 (Backspace) read 0x00000000 on the Fn layer while neighbouring keys carry tag 8? Is a missing tag-8 value the correct 'no Fn action' encoding, or is it corruption?
3. Capture a known-good Fn layer from a factory-fresh K1 Pro (without cmd-17 reset on the daily driver) and commit it as a fixture.

Blocked on hardware access; until resolved, tag 0x08 is opaque per §Safety 7.

title: remap-ui: stop exposing unknown-tag slots as editable
description:
Follow-on from AGENTS.md §Safety 7. web/src/remap.ts renders every keymap slot as editable and lets the pool overwrite it. On the K1 Pro Fn layer (arg 0x01) all the tag-0x08 action keys render as raw hex (0x08030200 ...) and can be rebound — losing an action the vendor UI itself cannot express or restore.

Also relevant: arg 4-7 (system bit) reads return a shifted/garbage payload (marker 5A A5 lands mid-table, bytes look rotated: 0x29000000 vs 0x00000029). The 'System keys' toggle in remap.ts:511 puts the user straight into editing that garbage, with write-back verified.

Acceptance criteria:
1. Slots whose value decodes to KeyValue::Unknown are shown as locked/opaque (label = raw hex + 'opaque'), not selectable as an edit target.
2. Args whose base read fails the keymap-base-guard (see keymap-base-guard bead) are not editable at all.
3. Selecting a pool key for an opaque slot is refused with an explanation.
4. Investigate the arg 4-7 read shape before re-enabling the System toggle — either fix the arg encoding or remove the toggle until the vendor's read for system layouts is understood.

title: fn-layer-doctor: read-only diagnostic for 'Fn key does nothing'

2. Flag slots carrying tag 0x08 with an 'opaque' note.
3. Cross-check the Fn key itself (arg 0, slot 59 on K1 Pro = 0x0D000000) exists in the base layer.
4. Report a verdict: 'Fn layer intact' vs 'N keys have no Fn action: ...'.

Wire it as 'omg kb916 doctor fn' (or 'omg diagnose fn') and surface the same result in the web dashboard. Explicitly must NOT offer or suggest cmd-17 reset.
